                            LIMITED PROTEST AND COMMENTS OF
                          CONSTELLATION ENERGY GENERATION, LLC

           Constellation1 submits this limited protest and comments in response to the PJM

Compliance Filing.2 Two aspects of the PJM Compliance Filing are non-compliant with the

June 2026 Co-Location Order.3 First, PJM has not shown that its proposal to delay the availability

of Interim Network Integration Transmission Service (“Interim NITS”) until July 1, 2028, is just




1
    Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (“Constellation”) files this limited protest and comments pursuant to Rule 211
    of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure. 18 C.F.R. § 385.211 (2026).
2
    Compliance Filing of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. in Response to Order on Rehearing, Clarification, Compliance
    Filing and Paper Hearing in Docket No. EL25-49-002, et al. (Aug. 17, 2026) (“PJM Compliance Filing”).
3
    PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 195 FERC ¶ 61,209 (2026) (“June 2026 Co-Location Order”).
 and reasonable.4 PJM has not explained with any specificity why it will take nearly two more years

to implement the service the Commission ordered in December 2025. Second, PJM has not

adequately explained the Necessary Study process for Interconnection Customers with existing or

ongoing Necessary Studies, as the Commission directed.5 PJM should be required to confirm that

customers can rely on the results of prior Necessary Studies where the scope has not changed.

           Three areas of the PJM Compliance Filing require clarification or further Commission

direction. First, PJM should clarify the meaning of “partial NITS” and its ability to immediately

provide that service. Second, PJM has added as a prerequisite for Interim NITS the “satisfaction

of any technical requirements identified by the applicable Transmission Owner(s).”6 This

condition requires reasonable limitations to prevent further Transmission Owner-driven delays in

providing service. Finally, the Commission should clarify that Interim NITS service cannot be

conditioned on resource adequacy considerations outside of real-time operational necessities.7

                                                     PROTEST

     I.    PJM’s Proposal to Delay the Availability of Interim NITS to July 1, 2028, Is Not Just
           and Reasonable

           The Commission should reject PJM’s proposal to delay Interim NITS Service until July 1,

2028, as PJM has not established that such a prolonged implementation period is just and

reasonable. First, PJM fails to “provide[] sufficient information” for the Commission to find such

 a delay to be just and reasonable.8 The Commission directed that PJM give “serious consideration”

to the proposed effective date given the “urgent” nature of large load interconnections.9 Yet PJM

justifies its July 1, 2028 implementation date in one conclusory sentence: “PJM Operations

personnel will need to implement additional tools and processes before they will be able to monitor

and curtail, as needed, the new non-firm Interim NITS product proposed in Tariff, Part XI.”10 That

is wholly inadequate. PJM still has not adequately considered “whether Interim NITS … can be

made effective at an earlier date,” as the Commission ordered it to do.11 As the June 2026 Co-

Location Order explains, the Commission “requires more support for the timeliness of a proposed

effective date.”12

            Second, PJM’s vague claim that its Operations personnel will need until July 1, 2028, to

“implement additional tools and processes” for Interim NITS is hard to square with PJM’s

assertion that it can implement Interim Resource Adequacy Service (“IRAS”) by June 1, 2027,

less than 10 months after being proposed.13 PJM fails to show that implementing Interim NITS

would be any more challenging than implementing IRAS. To implement IRAS, PJM must

establish a Large Load Registry, a new “database of information pertaining to Large Loads that

will be established and maintained by PJM.”14 PJM will use the Large Load Registry to “identify,

be called upon to reduce load.”15 During emergency conditions, “PJM will instruct Electric

Distributors to reduce load by a MW quantity equal to or less than the Electric Distributor’s

Eligible New Large Load Amount.”16 In addition, the Electric Distributors must “coordinate, as

appropriate, with the relevant state(s) or RERRA(s), individual Load Serving Entities, and

customers ... to support transparent, effective, and orderly deployment of [IRAS].”17 PJM does not

explain how long that coordination process will take or what it will entail. Nonetheless, PJM

proposes to implement IRAS by June 1, 2027, so that “coordination” process must be completed

in a matter of months.

            These IRAS requirements appear comparable to, if not more complicated (given the

involvement of numerous entities other than PJM) than what PJM claims is necessary for Interim

NITS: establishing additional tools and processes to monitor and curtail the service. For IRAS,

those tools and processes include the Large Load Registry and determination of each Electric

Distributor’s Eligible New Large Load Amount. And IRAS may in fact be more complicated

because it also requires the coordination process between the Electric Distributors, thirteen states

and others to determine “under their own laws, policies, and definition of what constitutes ‘large

load’—which resources will be called on to reduce load.”18

            In the interest of efficiency, the Commission should exercise its authority under

Section 206 of the Federal Power Act to fix a replacement rate and direct PJM to (i) adopt June 1,

 2027, as the date for implementing Interim NITS or (ii) demonstrate that it cannot meet that date

and propose the earliest possible date that it can meet. Implementing Interim NITS by June 1,

2027, is just and reasonable as it would remedy an unlawful rate within approximately 18 months

of the Commission’s finding. If PJM elects the latter, PJM should provide specific and detailed

comments explaining why June 1, 2027, is not feasible and identify all work streams PJM is

advancing before the availability of Interim NITS.

 II.        PJM Fails to Specify the Process for Interconnection Customers with Existing or
            Ongoing Necessary Studies

            PJM fails to address the Commission’s finding that “PJM’s proposed revisions lack clarity

with respect to how they apply to Interconnection Customers that have already executed Necessary

Study Agreements.”19 As the June 2026 Co-Location Order found, the “scope” of the Necessary

Studies “has not changed.”20 And PJM has not “otherwise demonstrate[d]” why “Interconnection

Customers seeking to serve Co-Located Load cannot rely on the results of Necessary Studies that

have already been performed if the scope of the study has not changed.”21

            The Commission should specifically order PJM to clarify that Necessary Studies need not

be repeated where their scope is the same as previously conducted Necessary Studies. The

Necessary Studies process can take years.22 Requiring duplicative studies without justification

would unnecessarily delay the interconnection of large loads and cannot be just and reasonable.

                                              CLARIFICATION

     I.    PJM’s Comment That It Can Provide “Partial NITS” Requires Further Explanation

           On compliance, PJM states that “[a]t present, PJM can provide partial NITS, i.e., NITS in

an amount less than requested and/or for a term shorter than requested, to Co-Located Load

through the Necessary Study process and therefore is proposing an October 17, 2026 effective

date for the bulk of the revisions proposed in this filing.”23 The Commission should require PJM

to clarify several aspects of this proposal.

           First, PJM should clarify what “partial NITS” is, whether it is a new or existing

transmission service, and which revisions are included in “the bulk.”

           Second, PJM should clarify its reference to the Necessary Study process, as it is unclear

how that process applies to PJM’s provision of “partial NITS” or Interim NITS. As the

Commission explained, “the studies applicable to a transmission service request … are distinct

from the Necessary Study process, which studies the modification of a generator

interconnection.”24 In addition to explaining what it means, PJM also should clarify that the

Necessary Study process can proceed at the same time as the study process for NITS and Interim

NITS conducted by PJM. This is particularly appropriate when the co-location arrangement

subject to the Necessary Study is one that will use NITS and Interim NITS services, which will

not require delisting of the generator. This in turn will make it much less likely that the results

would identify additions, modifications, or replacements to the Transmission System necessary




23

24

                                                        6
 to maintain system reliability.25 Interim NITS is an entirely front-of-the-meter service where

PJM will ultimately serve the entire load when standard NITS can be provided.

            Constellation emphasizes that even under ideal conditions, PJM’s Necessary Study

process takes 270 days,26 and in practice, the process often takes much longer.27 Conditioning the

provision of Interim NITS on the Necessary Studies could cause significant delay, making it

even more important that the implementation date be June 1, 2027.

 II.        Transmission Owner Technical Requirements Should Be Subject to Reasonable
            Limitations

            PJM’s proposed Section 702.4 adds “satisfaction of any technical requirements identified

by the applicable Transmission Owner(s)” as a “Technical Requirement[] Prior to Commencement

of Service.”28 This requirement was not included in PJM’s Initial Brief,29 nor did the June 2026

Co-Location Order require PJM to add it.30

            While Transmission Owners have a role in determining whether Interim NITS can be

reliably provided, reasonable processes and limitations on Transmission Owner-imposed technical

requirements are necessary to ensure that Eligible Customers taking Interim NITS are not subject

requirement late in the process, further delaying the availability of Interim NITS. Reasonable

limitations should include requiring Transmission Owners to identify applicable technical

requirements at the time they provide feedback on transmission studies, requiring all Transmission

Owner technical requirements to be on file with the Commission,31 and prohibiting Transmission

Owners from imposing technical requirements that are duplicative of PJM’s technical

requirements where redundancy is not justified.32

III.        PJM May Not Condition the Availability of Interim NITS on Resource Adequacy
            Considerations

            Constellation is concerned that PJM’s proposed tariff revisions will allow for anticipated

resource adequacy concerns to form a basis for denying or limiting Interim NITS requests. That

would be contrary to the Commission’s intent. As the Commission explained, “PJM will not

consider Interim NITS … in its resource adequacy planning.”33 The Commission recognized that

“increasing amounts of new Co-Located Load seeking to be served by an Eligible Customer faster

than equivalent generation can come online may create resource adequacy problems,”34 but found

 that Eligible Customers should be able to take service on behalf of Co-Located Loads that are

“willing and able to limit their energy withdrawals from the transmission system under certain

conditions.”35 The solution was not to bar Co-Located Loads from being timely served but to allow

Interim NITS and other interruptible services and curtail when circumstances required.

            Nevertheless, two tariff provisions raise this concern that PJM may attempt to condition

Interim NITS on anticipated resource adequacy shortfalls. Section 702.3 provides that PJM will

determine the amount of Interim NITS that “can be provided reliably … while maintaining the

reliability of the Transmission System” based on study procedures in “Tariff, Part XI, Subpart A,

Section 704”36—yet that section in turn states only that PJM will determine whether “additional

studies are needed” and if so, PJM will inform the “Eligible Customer of those studies as soon as

practicable.”37 Section 705.1 provides that PJM may “curtail Interim NITS for capacity or reserve

shortages as further set forth in the PJM Manuals”38 but does not identify the particular Manual or

specify that it is referring to real-time capacity or reserve shortages. The Commission should

confirm that a projection of resource adequacy is not a prerequisite for finding that PJM can

reliably provide Interim NITS.

                                                    CONCLUSION

            For the foregoing reasons, Constellation requests that the Commission require PJM to:

(1) make Interim NITS available by June 1, 2027, or explain why it cannot and propose the earliest



     Located Load are needed with respect to capacity market rules, reliability, and resource adequacy to ensure that the
     PJM Tariff remains just and reasonable”).

Necessary Studies sufficiently cover the circumstance; (3) clarify the meaning of “partial NITS”

and its proposal to provide that service immediately; (4) impose reasonable limitations on

Transmission Owner technical requirements; and (5) implement its proposed tariff in a manner

that does not use resource adequacy as a basis for denying or limiting Interim NITS requests.
